successCriteria.description: The `Notification` entity's `type` field is typed as `NotificationType` (imported from `../../shared/types`), not `string`.
The `Notification` entity's `status` field is typed as `NotificationStatus` (imported from `../../shared/types`), not `string`.

The `INotificationRepository.create` parameter type uses `NotificationType` for `type` and `NotificationStatus` for `status` in the `Omit<Notification, 'id' | 'createdAt'>` expansion — i.e., the create input is consistent with the entity's enum-typed fields.

The `INotificationService` method signatures (notifyLeaveSubmitted, notifyLeaveApproved, notifyLeaveRejected, notifyLeaveCancelled) return `Promise<Notification>` where `Notification.type` is `NotificationType` and `Notification.status` is `NotificationStatus` — the return type is consistent with the fixed entity.

constraints: Only the `Notification` entity interface and the `INotificationRepository` / `INotificationService` interfaces in `src/modules/notification/notification.model.ts` are modified. No new files are created. No concrete implementations (repository, service) are written — those belong to Phase 6.
The `NotificationType` and `NotificationStatus` enums in `src/shared/types/index.ts` are NOT modified — they are already correct and are the authoritative source.
The existing `import { NotificationStatus } from '../../shared/types'` in notification.model.ts must be extended to also import `NotificationType`. No other imports change.
outOfScope: Creating or modifying concrete implementations (PgNotificationRepository, NotificationService) — deferred to Phase 6.
Creating or modifying notification tests — deferred to Phase 6.
Changing any other entity's field types (LeaveRequest, Balance, LeavePolicy, Employee, AuditLog) — only the Notification entity is in scope.

ambiguities.description: The `INotificationRepository.findByRecipientIdAndStatus` and `INotificationRepository.updateStatus` already use `NotificationStatus` in their parameter types — this is correct and consistent with the fix. No ambiguity about whether those signatures should also change.
options: Keep repository method signatures as-is (they already use NotificationStatus)
Also change repository method signatures (unnecessary — they are already correct)

entityInvariants.invariant: Every Notification instance MUST have a `type` value that is a member of the `NotificationType` enum (leave_submitted | leave_approved | leave_rejected | leave_cancelled) and a `status` value that is a member of the `NotificationStatus` enum (pending | sent | read | archived). This is enforced at compile time by the TypeScript type system.

The `Notification` entity's `type` and `status` fields are the single source of truth for notification typing. Any code that creates or consumes a Notification (repository implementations, service implementations, controllers) MUST derive the field types from the entity interface, not from local string literals or casts.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth rule — repository interfaces are internal; auth is enforced at the controller/route layer.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the created Notification with enum-typed `type` and `status` fields. The input parameter's `type` and `status` fields must accept `NotificationType` and `NotificationStatus` enum values respectively.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The `Notification.type` field type MUST be `NotificationType` as defined and exported from `src/shared/types/index.ts`. The entity must import and use the enum, not a string literal or locally-defined type.

The `Notification.status` field type MUST be `NotificationStatus` as defined and exported from `src/shared/types/index.ts`. The entity must import and use the enum, not a string literal or locally-defined type.

integrationPoints.target: src/modules/leave-request/leave-request.model.ts (INotificationService is referenced in ILeaveRequestService constructor — Phase 6 implementation)
integrationPoints.why: The leave-request service depends on INotificationService. When Phase 6 implements LeaveRequestService, it will consume the fixed Notification entity with enum-typed fields. No action needed now — the fix is forward-compatible.
